title: DM-LFM West-German reunification gold from pblasso 1.0.8, plus the paper's single-treated-unit Monte Carlo
paper: Pang, X., Liu, L., & Xu, Y. (2022), 'A Bayesian Alternative to Synthetic Control for Comparative Case Studies', Political Analysis 30(2):269-288; Abadie, Diamond & Hainmueller (2015) for the German reunification data
reference_impl: R package pblasso 1.0.8, shipped in the authors' replication package (packages/pblasso_1.0.8.tar.gz). This is the version behind the published figures; the public liulch/bpCausal repository is a later rename and is NOT the same code.
status: active -- the oracle for mlsynth.DMLFM; the comparison lives in benchmarks/cases/dmlfm_germany.py

outputs.gold_summary.csv: per-seed overall ATT, credible interval, pre-treatment gap summaries, sigma2, runtime
outputs.gold_att_by_year.csv: per-seed, per-year ATT with 95% credible bounds
outputs.gold_counterfactual.csv: per-seed observed and posterior-mean counterfactual GDP for West Germany
outputs.gold_omega_gamma.csv: per-seed posterior mean and deciles of |omega_gamma|, the factor-loading scales that drive factor selection
outputs.gold_covariates.csv: the six time-invariant covariates as the authors construct them
outputs.montecarlo_single_treated.csv: the authors' own saved Monte Carlo output (tempdata/sim_single_{X,r3,r8}.RData): bias, sd, RMSE, coverage and runtime for synth, gsynth and the Bayesian DM-LFM across 3 designs x 6 cases

targets.tolerance_note: MCMC noise only, ten seeds at niter=25000, burn=5000. The spread is wide relative to the effect: compare a port on means across several seeds, not on a single run. An eight-seed port run agreeing at Welch p=0.16 with variances agreeing at F-test p=0.42 reproduces the estimator.
